Dunno what broken ORMs everyone is using, but every one I've ever used has given me enough control to pretty much exactly control what SQL is going to be run. So I get good performance on the database side, while still being able to implement my object-oriented program with objects.

FWIW, I use DBIx::Class.

I also agree that ORMs are a bad fit for many programs. Most of the applications that people are writing don't need a relational database at all, as arbitrary queries wouldn't make much sense. In that case, you might as well use an object database -- then there is no querying and there is no impedance mismatch. The result is an app that runs fast and is fast to implement.
